messages:
maria: FYI canary showing short SSE pauses (~5-7s). Clients reconnect with same resume token but billing logs show a new generation event on resume, doubling cost for affected requests.

raj: Do we see proxy 204s or socket closes?

maria: Proxy emits a 204 during the hold. Client then reconnects with resume token. Upstream sees resume but billing path treats it as a new gen.

jordan: Console traces show route_key flips at the same time. Looks like proxy may be dropping an affinity header on 204.

sam: Can we reproduce with a dev flag?

maria: Yes: PROXY_SIMULATE_MIDSTREAM_204=true in staging reproduces.

raj: Short-term: add per-request trace flag to surface "resume vs reconnect" so SREs can tell. Long-term: patch proxy to preserve x-resume-id and route-affinity across 204/hold.

jordan: I'll add a canary telemetry tile: resume_vs_new_gen and alert on >5% deviation. Also add duplicate_token_event graph per tenant.

ops-bot: [alert] 1749999030 - reconnect spike: tenant=acme-co +280% in 5m

sam: Pushing tiny proxy build fix (branch fix/proxy-preserve-resume-headers) to canary now.

maria: Quick checks: header preserved, route_key stable, billing no longer emits extra generation for resumed streams.

sam: Deploy started canary-2026-03-22-17 by sam at 1749999045

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded at 1749999060

raj: Next steps: add rollout health metric (resume_success_rate) into canary scoring; add playbook check to validate resume headers during rollouts.

maria: If any edge cases remain we'll consider a short debounce in billing as fallback, but prefer fixing header preservation. :thumbsup:
